newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real off 0.05 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real off 0.05 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.05 percent to end at 1.0211 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank fixed a weaker mini-band for the local currency at 1.021 to 1.026 reais per dollar.
The real fell 0.45 percent during the month of September.

The Central Bank set the new real-dollar mini-band through a buy/sell auction shortly after the open. The previous trade level was set on Friday at between 1.0205 and 1.0255 reais to the dollar. The mini-band was lowered 0.5 during this month.

The Central Bank bought dollars twice at 1.0210 reais per greenback to drain the excess dollars which entered the market last week, when commercial and financial forex contracts registered a surplus of around $533 million.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real dipped 0.02 percent to end at 1.0266 to the dollar. In September, the real fell 0.54 percent in the floating market.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended at 1.040 real per dollar, down 0.19 percent for the day and 1.07 percent for the month, traders said.
